newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Japanese Prime Minister urges calm in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Japanese Prime Minister urges calm in Cambodia.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has written a letter to Cambodia's political leaders expressing "strong concern" over political tension in the Southeast Asian nation, senior officials said on Saturday.

Three copies of the letter were delivered to co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and acting head of state Chea Sim on Saturday by Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs Masahiko Koumura, officials said.
"It was a letter of strong concern," said Ranariddh's chief of cabinet Ly Thuch.

"First, (it addressed) the killing on the 30th of March and second, the instability in Cambodia. (Hashimoto) urged in the first case to find the killers of the innocent people and in the second case (asked the co-premiers) to pledge to do their best to cooperate," he said.
A spokesman for Hun Sen confirmed the co-premier had also received the letter but declined to comment further.
Analysts said the letter carried extra weight as Japan is the leading donor nation to Cambodia, providing nearly $500 million in aid since 1991.

The troubled relationship between Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, has grown increasingly acrimonious since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration led by opposition leader and Ranariddh ally Sam Rainsy.
The tensions worsened last week when Hun Sen said he supported a challenge to Ranariddh's leadership by royalist dissidents, sparking rumours of an imminent coup.
